newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arafat receives presidential welcome in Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Arafat receives presidential welcome in Jordan.

text.p: King Hussein gave Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat a presidential welcome on Saturday when he arrived on a one-day visit to brief Jordan on stalled peace talks with Israel, officials said.

Arafat, who flew from Gaza in a Jordanian helicopter that landed on the grounds of Amman's Royal Raghdan Palace was given a full guards of honour welcome by the king, Crown Prince Hassan and Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti.
The Palestinian leader's ceremonial welcome was another sign of stepped-up public show of support for Arafat in his tough negotiations with Israel, officials said.
Arafat is usually received with minimal pomp during his frequent short visits to Jordan to brief King Hussein on peace talks with Israel.

Officials say the warmer ties with Arafat reflect the king's growing exasperation with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Middle East policies that the kingdom fears endangers its own stability.

Jordanian-Palestinian ties, which have traditionally been marred by rivalry, have significantly improved since Amman began accusing Israel of foot-dragging on implementing peace accords with the Palestinians.
Jordan squarely blames Israel for lack of tangible progress in talks with the Palestinians over a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron.
